blindSummary:
This state/province led the national statistics for 2025 with 7 recorded killings of LGBT+ people; trans women made up 58.3% of all such killings nationwide that year, across at least 17 reporting states/provinces. Its 2021 legal-gender-recognition law imposed an 18-year-old minimum that the national high court voided in March 2022, yet the legislature has still not corrected the text — legislative non-compliance with a final court ruling is itself a hostility signal directly relevant to a visitor whose documents need to match presentation.

No dedicated investigative machinery, no transfeminicide offence, no enforcement data at state/province level. The combination of top-of-table lethality and open defiance of the judiciary distinguishes this state/province from states/provinces that simply lack statutes; here a statute exists but the legislature actively refuses to conform it to a binding ruling.

Local risk sits below the country-wide average. Compared with the country's capital district, which also had high 2024-25 counts but created a transfeminicide unit and protocol within months, this state/province has neither the legal correction nor any enforcement innovation. Compared with a neighbouring state/province, which also defies a national high-court ruling on recognition but at least has had a hate-crime provision since 2021, this state/province has neither the court compliance nor the criminal-law protection.
